newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open lower.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open lower.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious were called to open lower Wednesday as Tuesday's shortcovering bounce in gold faded and selling resumed in Asia and Europe.

"Initial support is still seen around $312.00 an ounce, but the big number that may attract some serious bargain hunting from Asian and Middle Eastern buyers and some shortcovering is likely to be ultimately around $300-305 an ounce," a bullion banker said.
COMEX August gold was called down $2.00 to $3.00 from Tuesday's close of $321.00 after trading from $320.90 to 316.20 on ACCESS.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $317.00/50 early after hitting a new 12-year low fix of $315.75 in London this morning. In New York Tuesday, spot gold ended quoted at $319.80/$320.30.
Implied lease rates for gold rose further early today to more than 2.00 percent in most maturities, as producers borrowed gold to hedge and funds borrowed to fund short positions.
COMEX gold stocks rose 43,439 ounces to 881,747 ounces Tuesday, while COMEX silver stocks fell 1,346,606 ounces to 181,476,841 ounces.
COMEX September silver was called down 2.00 to 3.00 cents from Tuesday's close of $4.335 after setting record volume of 1,222 contracts on ACCESS. It traded between $4.335 and $4.250.
NYMEX October platinum was called off $1.00 to $2.00 from the previous close of $386.50, with NYMEX September palladium called down the same from Tuesday's close of $163.75.
Spot platinum fixed at $399.00 in London this morning, down from $409.00 at the previous fix, ahead of the expected resumption of Russian exports this week.
